name: Kayak with a proper forward stroke
blurb: Nearly everyone paddles a kayak with their arms and wonders why it hurts. The forward stroke comes from torso rotation, and getting that right doubles your range.
gear: A kayak and a correctly sized paddle
steps: Set up: sit upright with your back off the seat back, knees braced against the hull, feet on the pegs.
Learn the forward stroke: plant the blade fully near your feet, then rotate your torso to pull the boat past the blade. Your arms mostly hold their shape.
Exit the stroke at your hip. Pulling past the hip lifts water and steers you off course.
Learn the sweep stroke for turning and the low brace for stability.
Practise a wet exit in shallow, warm water with someone present — knowing you can get out calmly removes the fear that makes everything harder.
Learn to read wind and current before going anywhere committing.
tips: Sore arms and shoulders mean you are not rotating. Sore torso means you are doing it right.
Always wear a buoyancy aid and tell someone your plan. Cold water incapacitates fast.
proof: You paddle five kilometres in a straight line, comfortably, and can wet-exit and re-enter calmly.
